lines.speaker: control
lines.text: Anchor twenty-two. A hundred megawatts. Nothing on survey but the usual.

lines.speaker: okonkwo
lines.text: Four hours. I've been reading the maintenance logs. Somebody here was replacing the same coupling every eleven days for two hundred years.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: That's not a person. That's a machine with a work order.

lines.speaker: okonkwo
lines.text: It logged the part number wrong twice and corrected itself. Machines don't do that.
lines.beat: the act's quiet one — the wardens become almost sympathetic here

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: My sister keeps asking what the sky looks like out here.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: That it's fine. There isn't one, but it's fine.

lines.speaker: okonkwo
lines.text: Two hundred years of eleven-day intervals, Vasquez. Whoever wrote that rota is long dead and the rota is still running.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: So are we, eventually. Doesn't mean we stop.

lines.speaker: okonkwo
lines.text: Over budget. Not badly — but it's costing you across the board.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: Tighten up. This one was supposed to be easy.

lines.speaker: okonkwo
lines.text: I logged the coupling. Eleven days from now it'll want doing again and there'll be nobody on this anchor to do it.

lines.speaker: vasquez
lines.text: You want to leave a note?

lines.speaker: okonkwo
lines.text: I did. Part number and the interval. It'll be wrong in a year and it took me thirty seconds.
lines.beat: the sympathy lands here — he does the dead crew's paperwork and does not explain why
